analysis:
Examined docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (base/head; head adds the `coordinator traffic` doctor check at L83 and an expanded no-traffic recovery row at L143) and the new provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Coordinator/UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift (L1-50). Only metadata was supplied for ServingReadiness.swift (unit 47f42b08690f9b5f:0). Its head text was absent apart from a truncated orientation excerpt, so verdict logic is unverified. The excerpt states that it is diagnostics-only and that the coordinator owns routing and authorization.

UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery is a pure timing policy for provider-initiated re-registration. It starts after 15 minutes plus a per-process jitter of 0-15 minutes (L15-17, L27-28). Retries back off at 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, then every 4 h (L33-36), which matches doc L143. It runs only when the provider is not busy (L27). connectionLacksAuthorization (L42-49) treats these as unauthorized:
- untrusted or offline status;
- no status after ServingReadiness.statusGraceSeconds (90 s per the excerpt);
- an expired App Attest authorization when the path is not legacy.

This grants no trust locally. A re-registration starts a fresh coordinator verification session, and coordinator authorization stays authoritative (TB-002, TB-011, T-052, T-053). An adversarial provider could already reconnect at will, so this adds no capability for ADV-001. The backoff and jitter limit fleet reconnect storms, which is relevant to availability under T-057.

No regression was identified.

Integration questions:
1. Confirm that the callers in ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift compute `busy` to include accepted or local requests, model loads, Autopilot, drain and update. This matters so that a reconnect cannot drop in-flight encrypted work (T-010, T-053).
2. Confirm that a reconnect does not reuse a stale grant and follows the existing endpoint-resumption and binding rules (T-053, A-016).
3. Confirm that an add-on hold (TB-012, T-059) suppresses or interacts correctly with forced re-registration.
4. Confirm that ServingReadiness and the doctor/status output do not log sensitive authorization identifiers (T-058).
